info.title: sigiro API Reference
info.description: Send OpenTelemetry to sigiro. Ask what changed. Get ranked findings and the SQL that proves them.

post.description: Accept a Pyroscope PushRequest or raw pprof profile. With `name`, the payload is raw pprof and the service name is the part before the first `{`; without `name`, the payload is a PushRequest whose series require a `service_name` label. Binary bodies may be gzip-compressed. Multipart bodies must carry the payload in the `profile` field. A missing Content-Type is also accepted as a binary body. See the [profile ingest guide](https://sigiro.com/docs/how-to/send-profiles).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
When present, the body is a raw pprof profile and the service name is the
part before the first `{`. When absent, the body is a Pyroscope
PushRequest and each series must contain a `service_name` label.

requestBody.description: Pyroscope PushRequest or raw pprof bytes. For multipart/form-data, put the binary payload in the `profile` field.

400.description: Unsupported media type, malformed payload, missing service name, or empty profile

413.description: Request body exceeds the configured ingest limit

get.description: Precomputed anomalies: worsening regime shifts (BOCPD changepoints, threshold-free) detected continuously over persisted 5-minute series of every signal — error_rate and latency_p95 per operation, log_volume, error_log_rate and profile_cost (the service's total profiled cost) per service (the `operation` field holds the entity) — and persisted to the `sigiro_anomalies` table. Ordered by the unit-free shift magnitude (after - before) / (after + before) descending (1.0 = appeared from a zero baseline, 1/3 = doubled), so the most significant shifts lead regardless of the signal's units — nothing is filtered out; judge significance from `before`/`after` (raw signal units: %, µs, logs, profile cost). Optionally filter by `service` and a `from_ts`/`to_ts` window (microseconds since the Unix epoch) over the shift time. Each row carries a ready-to-run `drill_down_sql` for POST /v1/query. Rows whose shifts fall in the same or adjacent 5-minute detection bucket on the same service share an `incident_id` — one incident across signals, not N independent anomalies (the correlation window is the detection pass's own bucket resolution, never a tuned threshold); `incident_id` is null for uncorrelated rows. `truncated` is true when the query row cap omitted shifts: this is an incomplete candidate snapshot and automatic submission must wait for a complete response.

parameters.name: from_ts
parameters.description: Only shifts at or after this time (microseconds since the Unix epoch).

parameters.name: to_ts
parameters.description: Only shifts at or before this time (microseconds since the Unix epoch).

post.description: Root-cause an incident for one or more services over a time window. Returns a triage summary — NOT raw telemetry: a ranked `findings` array (read this first), per-operation anomaly flags, and bounded samples of spans/logs. Every lead carries a ready-to-run SQL string (`drill_down_sql` on standalone findings, each incident member shift, operations, spans, and log patterns; `drill_all_sql` on the spans/logs sections) that you paste VERBATIM into `POST /v1/query` to fetch the underlying rows and go deeper. Typical agent loop: `GET /v1/services` → `POST /v1/diagnose` → for any standalone finding, incident member shift, or anomalous operation, run its `drill_down_sql` via `/v1/query`. Timestamps are microseconds since the Unix epoch. The response is a map `{results: {service: block}, errors: {service: message}}` — partial results survive a single failing service.

400.description: Invalid request (e.g. timestamps not in microseconds, or to_ts <= from_ts)

post.description:
Every `drill_down_sql` that `/v1/diagnose` returns can be pasted here
verbatim.

Readable tables, optionally qualified `lake.*` or `main.*`:

- `sigiro_spans`
- `sigiro_logs`
- `sigiro_metrics_gauge`
- `sigiro_metrics_sum`
- `sigiro_metrics_histogram`
- `sigiro_metrics_exp_histogram`
- `sigiro_profiles`
- `sigiro_anomalies`

## Bound `timestamp` with a literal, not `now()`

Statistics pruning only happens when the comparison value is a constant the
planner can fold. `now()` is volatile, so any predicate built from it is
evaluated per row and every file in the table is opened.

```sql
-- prunes: the planner folds the constant and skips whole files
WHERE timestamp > TIMESTAMP '2026-08-31 08:00:00'

-- does not prune: opens every file, then filters
WHERE timestamp > (now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR)::TIMESTAMP
```

Compute the bound in your client and send it as a literal.

## If you must use `now()`, cast it

The `timestamp` columns are `TIMESTAMP` (no timezone) and `now()` returns
`TIMESTAMPTZ`. Comparing them directly makes DuckDB cast the **column**,
which adds a per-row conversion on top of the missing pruning. Measured
against production on 2026-08-31, same table and window:

| predicate | result |
|---|---|
| `timestamp > TIMESTAMP '2026-08-31 08:00:00'` | 200 in 2.48s |
| `timestamp > (now() - INTERVAL 5 MINUTE)::TIMESTAMP` | 200 in 0.65s |
| `timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 5 MINUTE` | 400 `INTERRUPT` at 10.98s |
| `timestamp > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-31 08:00:00+00'` | 400 `INTERRUPT` at 10.65s |

So the cast is worth having, but it is a mitigation and not the fix: the
literal is.

requestBody.description: One SELECT statement. No WITH/CTE clauses — rewrite them as derived-table subqueries. Scalar functions are allowlisted; file and network readers are blocked. Bound timestamp columns with a literal TIMESTAMP rather than an expression built from now(), or statistics pruning is lost and the query reads every file.

text/plain.example: SELECT service_name, count(*) AS errors FROM sigiro_spans WHERE status_code = 2 AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2026-09-11 12:00:00' AND timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2026-09-11 13:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

200.description: Query results — one object per row, keyed by your SELECT's column names

get.description: Every service that has reported telemetry, with the first and last timestamp seen for each (microseconds since the Unix epoch). The entry point of an agent loop: pick a service here, then diagnose it.
Every span of one trace, parent links included, so a caller can rebuild the tree. Trace IDs come from the sampled spans in a diagnosis, or from any SQL query over `sigiro_spans`.

AnomaliesResponse.description:
GET /v1/anomalies — precomputed regime shifts of every signal from the
continuous anomaly pass (the `sigiro_anomalies` table), biggest shift
first by the unit-free magnitude (after − before) / (after + before)
(comparable across signals; raw |after − before| breaks zero-baseline
ties, then newest first). Ranking, not filtering: the reader judges
significance from `before`/`after`. `truncated` reports the query row cap.

truncated.description:
True when the query row cap omitted shifts. This is an incomplete
candidate snapshot: automatic submission must wait for a complete one.

AnomalyEntry.description:
One row of the `sigiro_anomalies` table: a worsening regime shift found
by BOCPD changepoint detection over an entity's continuous 5-minute
series. No thresholds are involved anywhere — `direction` is always
"worsening" because only shifts whose mean after exceeds the mean
before are persisted.

after.description: Series mean from the shift onward.

before.description:
Series mean before the shift, raw signal units (error %, p95 µs,
logs per bucket, summed profile cost per bucket).

detected_at.description: When the scheduled pass wrote this row (ISO timestamp).

drill_down_sql.description:
Ready-to-run SQL for POST /v1/query: the raw telemetry behind the
shift (spans, logs, or profile samples, per the signal).

incident_id.description:
Cross-signal correlation id. Rows sharing an id shifted in the same
or adjacent 5-minute detection bucket on the same service — one
incident, not N independent anomalies (the window is the detection
pass's own bucket resolution, not a threshold). `null` when the row
correlates with no other returned row. Computed over the rows this
request returns, so `service`/window filters scope the grouping.

operation.description:
The entity the shifted series is keyed by: the derived operation
identity (error_rate / latency_p95 — matches
`operation_summaries[].operation` in /v1/diagnose) or the service
name (log_volume / error_log_rate / profile_cost).

ts_shift.description: First bucket of the NEW regime (ISO timestamp).

ts_shift_us.description:
`ts_shift` as µs since the Unix epoch — the value incident
correlation buckets on.

Coverage.description: Computed coverage for the diagnosis window.

signals.description: Signal coverage details instead of flat gap strings.

detected_at_us.description:
`detected_at` as µs since the Unix epoch — what incident correlation
aligns deploys against.

from_ts.description:
Window start, **microseconds** since the Unix epoch (a 16-digit value,
e.g. 1780000000000000). Seconds, milliseconds, and nanoseconds are rejected.
OPTIONAL: omit both `from_ts` and `to_ts` for the last 15 minutes, the
same default `sigiro diagnose` uses. Providing `to_ts` without `from_ts`
is rejected — a window that ends somewhere with no start is ambiguous,
and guessing one silently would answer a question nobody asked.

services.description:
Services to diagnose (1–10). Call `GET /v1/services` first to discover
valid names.

to_ts.description:
Window end, microseconds since the Unix epoch. Must be > `from_ts`.
Optional: defaults to now when `from_ts` is given alone.

DiagnoseResponse.description:
Response envelope for a diagnosis: per-service blocks plus
per-service failures. Partial results by design — one broken service
must not discard the other nine (fail loud, per service).

errors.description:
Services whose diagnosis query failed, keyed by service name,
with the error message. Empty when everything succeeded.

results.description: Successful diagnosis blocks, keyed by service name.

error_traces_total.description:
Distinct traces with an error span in the window — the headline
"something's wrong" signal. Drill via the anomalous `operation_summaries`
or the `spans` section, each of which carries a ready-to-run query.

findings.description:
Ranked list (critical first) of what deserves attention in this
window. Anomalies are CORRELATED across signals first: shifts in the
same or adjacent 5-minute detection bucket merge into one "incident"
finding bundling the member shifts and the suspect deploy; lone
shifts stay single-signal findings. Anomaly findings then rank by
(correlated signal count, unit-free shift magnitude
(after − before) / (after + before), raw |Δ|) descending — a
multi-signal incident outranks a lone shift; the magnitude is
comparable across error-rate, latency, log and profile shifts.
Non-anomaly findings (error/log inconsistencies, actionable coverage
gaps) follow. Read this before the raw sections below.

gen_ai.description:
Per-(provider, model) LLM stats from OTel GenAI (`gen_ai.*`) span
attributes, most-called first. Empty when the window has no LLM
spans — services that never call a model simply don't have this.

log_counters.description:
Numbers the service logs about itself, promoted to statistics — the
counters already embedded in log lines like
`enqueued=1024 responses=24 translations=0`, one row per number.
`pinned_zero` rows come first: a counter that never left zero while
another number on the SAME line did move. That is the signature of a
stage doing no work, which no baseline detector can find (a flat-zero
series has nothing to deviate from) and which looks identical to
"nothing to do".

log_patterns.description:
Log patterns (template-deduplicated, ordered by count). Each row carries
a `drill_down_sql` for its raw logs.

logs.description: Raw logs, newest first — a self-describing sample (see `spans`).

spans.description:
Top spans (errors first, then slowest), as a self-describing sample:
`total` vs the returned rows tells you how much was withheld, and
`drill_all_sql` fetches the rest.

ErrorTypeCount.description:
One failure mode of an operation's error spans: the OTel `error.type`
dimension (stable semconv) with the number of error spans carrying it.

count.description: Error spans of this operation carrying this failure mode.

error_type.description:
The `error.type` value, derived per span (see `error_type_expr`):
the span's real `error.type` attribute when emitted; else the HTTP
response status code (OTel's own rule for HTTP errors — "429",
"500"); else "timeout" when `status_message` mentions one; else
"_OTHER" (the semconv catch-all). Low-cardinality by construction.

severity.description: Findings are sorted critical, warning, then info.

summary.description: Human/agent-readable one-liner with the concrete numbers.

Finding.description:
One ranked, self-contained "what deserves attention" item — the first
thing an agent reads. Assembled in Rust from data the single query already
returned (zero extra SQL, zero extra memory).

FindingKind.description:
Closed finding categories with category-specific payloads. The internal
serde tag preserves the flat `kind` field while making an incident without
incident data, or incident data on another category, unrepresentable.

FinishReasonCount.description:
One finish-reason bucket of a model's LLM calls — the OTel
`gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` dimension ("stop", "length",
"tool_calls", "content_filter", "error").

count.description: LLM calls of this (system, model) that finished with this reason.

GenAiModelSummary.description:
Per-(provider, model) LLM call stats, read from the OTel GenAI semconv
(`gen_ai.*`, STABLE) span attributes. One row per (system, model) seen
in the window; a service that makes no LLM calls has none — the section
is simply empty. Threshold-free: ranked by call_count, nothing dropped.

call_count.description: LLM spans for this (system, model) in the window.

error_pct.description: Percentage of those spans with OTel status ERROR.

finish_reasons.description:
Finish-reason composition of this model's calls, biggest first —
a rising "length"/"content_filter" share is a failure mode
`error_pct` alone never shows. Empty when never emitted.

input_tokens.description:
Sum of `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` across calls that reported it;
None when no call did (distinct from a real 0).

operations.description:
Distinct `gen_ai.operation.name` values seen for this model
(e.g. "chat", "embeddings"), sorted. Empty when never emitted.

system.description:
The GenAI provider (`gen_ai.system`, e.g. "openai", "anthropic");
"unknown" when the SDK didn't emit it.

Incident.description:
Cross-signal correlation of the anomaly subsystem: N regime shifts whose
`ts_shift` fall in the same or adjacent detection bucket (the scheduled
pass's own 5-minute resolution — see `crate::anomaly::correlate_shifts`
for why that window is structural, not a threshold) on one service are
ONE incident, not N alerts. Nothing is dropped: every member shift is
listed with its own before → after and drill query.

oneOf.description:
The deploy that landed inside the incident's bucket span or in the
bucket immediately before its first shift — the prime suspect. None
when no deploy correlates.

shifts.description:
The correlated shifts, biggest first (by the same unit-free magnitude
findings are ranked by).

started_at.description:
Earliest member `ts_shift` — the first detection bucket of the
incident, µs since the Unix epoch.

IncidentShift.description:
One member shift of an [`Incident`] — the same row the anomaly pass
persisted, with its entity, numbers, and drill kept intact.

after.description: Series mean from the shift onward.

before.description: Series mean before the shift (raw signal units).

drill_down_sql.description: Ready-to-run /v1/query SQL for the raw telemetry behind this shift.

entity.description:
The shifted entity, e.g. "operation 'POST /pay'" (span signals) or
"service 'api'" (log/profile signals).

summary.description: The shift in prose, e.g. "error rate shifted at 14:30 (5.1% → 50.0%)".

ts_shift.description: First bucket of the new regime, µs since the Unix epoch.

LogCounter.description:
One number a service logs about itself, aggregated over the window.

Free metrics: DRAIN already masks numbers out of every log body to build the
template and keeps the original token in `template_values`, so each numeric
variable position is a time series nobody had to instrument. The label is the
masked template token itself (`translations=<NUM>`), which is why this needs
no naming heuristic.

label.description: The masked template token, e.g. `translations=<NUM>` — its own label.

pattern.description: The log template this number appears in.

pinned_zero.description:
Never left zero in the whole window, while another number on the same
log line did. Not ranked as an anomaly (a chronically-flat series is by
definition not a deviation) — it is stated so the question "should this
be zero?" gets asked. That question is the only thing that finds work
which was switched off before the retention window opened.

LogPattern.description: A log pattern with aggregated statistics.

drill_down_sql.description:
Pre-built SQL query the agent can run to fetch all raw logs matching
this pattern in chronological order. Filled in Rust (needs the caller's
window + service).

sample_values.description:
Up to 5 distinct extracted-variable tuples (each a JSON array of the
wildcard values for one log line) — enough to see what varies.

template_id.description: Stable template ID for compact grouping. None if no template was extracted.

anomaly_reason.description:
The detected shift(s) in prose, biggest shift (|after − before|)
first when there are several, e.g.
"error rate shifted at 14:32 (5.1% → 23.8%)" /
"p95 shifted at 14:30 (2.1s → 240.0s)".

drill_down_sql.description:
Ready-to-run query for the raw spans behind this operation (errors
first, then slowest). Sits next to `anomaly_reason` on purpose: when an
operation looks wrong, this is exactly how to pull the evidence. Filled
in Rust.

error_breakdown.description:
Failure-mode composition of this operation's error spans — the OTel
`error.type` dimension, biggest first (count desc, then name).
Answers HOW the operation fails (timeout vs 429 vs 500), not just
that it does — `error_pct` alone collapses 246 timeouts and 6 HTTP
500s into one number. Empty when the operation has no error spans.

is_anomalous.description:
Whether the continuous anomaly pass (augurs BOCPD changepoints over
this operation's persisted error-rate and p95-latency series — see
`crate::anomaly`) found a worsening regime shift (mean after > mean
before) whose `ts_shift` falls inside this diagnosis window. Read from the
`sigiro_anomalies` table, never recomputed per request. Improvements
do not flag, and a chronic-but-stable failure rate has no changepoint
and is NOT anomalous — it IS the baseline; read `error_pct` for
chronic health.

Not present in the SQL payload (filled in Rust from the joined
anomaly rows) — `default` keeps the flattened deserialize working.

operation.description:
The operation identity spans are grouped by. Usually equals
`span_name`, but generic HTTP spans (span_name is a bare method like
"POST", per OTel HTTP semconv) are disambiguated with
`http.route`/`server.address` from span_attributes — e.g.
"POST api.example.com" — so one giant "POST" bucket doesn't swallow
every outbound call.

span_name.description:
The raw OTel span name behind this operation (one representative
value when the group was derived from attributes).

SampledSection_LogRecord.description:
A bounded sample of a larger set that carries its own "there's more, and
here's how to get it" affordance, so an agent can decide to drill without
guessing. When `total > sample.len()`, run `drill_all_sql` via /v1/query.

drill_all_sql.description:
Query returning the full set for this section, ready to paste into
/v1/query.

sampled_by.description: How the sample was ordered/selected, e.g. "errors first, then slowest".

SampledSection_SpanRecord.description:
A bounded sample of a larger set that carries its own "there's more, and
here's how to get it" affordance, so an agent can decide to drill without
guessing. When `total > sample.len()`, run `drill_all_sql` via /v1/query.

drill_all_sql.description:
Query returning the full set for this section, ready to paste into
/v1/query.

items.description:
A flat span record. Attributes and events are embedded as real JSON
(not escaped strings) so agents can read them directly.

drill_down_sql.description:
Ready-to-run query for the full trace this span belongs to (every span
sharing its `trace_id`, chronological). Filled in Rust.

span_kind.description: OTel span kind as stored (integer enum).

status_message.description:
OTel status message — for spans that fail without emitting any log
(e.g. HTTP client errors) this is often the only diagnostic string.

sampled_by.description: How the sample was ordered/selected, e.g. "errors first, then slowest".

duration_us.description: Cumulative inclusive duration of the service's spans, in microseconds.

percentage.description: Percentage of cumulative inclusive span duration across all services.

pod_count.description:
F-26: distinct pod count when `service.instance.id` is present in
resource attributes, else 0. Use `has_instance_id` to distinguish
"no pods identified" from "service not seen".

ServiceDependency.description: Service dependency graph node with aggregated stats.

error_count.description: Number of error spans in shared traces.

span_count.description: Number of spans from this service in shared traces.

SignalCoverage.description: Signal availability for a given service/time range.

available.description: Whether this signal type has data in the window.

reason.description: Human-readable reason if not available, or summary if available.

SpanDetail.description: Individual span detail in trace detail response.

SpanRecord.description:
A flat span record. Attributes and events are embedded as real JSON
(not escaped strings) so agents can read them directly.

drill_down_sql.description:
Ready-to-run query for the full trace this span belongs to (every span
sharing its `trace_id`, chronological). Filled in Rust.

span_kind.description: OTel span kind as stored (integer enum).

status_message.description:
OTel status message — for spans that fail without emitting any log
(e.g. HTTP client errors) this is often the only diagnostic string.

TraceDetailResponse.description: Complete trace detail response with critical path and service breakdown.

total_duration_us.description: Elapsed wall-clock time from the earliest span start to the latest span end, in microseconds.
